{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
file_path = "/home/musel/Github/research_agent/data/sales.csv"
data = pd.read_csv(file_path)

# Inspect the data
print("Data shape:", data.shape)
print("\nFirst few rows:")
print(data.head())

print("\nColumn dtypes:")
print(data.dtypes)

print("\nMissing values:")
print(data.isnull().sum())

print("\nUnique values per column:")
print(data.nunique())

# Check for the six QA orders with revenue = 999999.99
qa_orders = data[data['revenue'] == '999999.99']
print(f"\nNumber of QA orders (revenue = 999999.99): {len(qa_orders)}")
print(qa_orders[['order_id', 'channel', 'customer_segment', 'customer_age', 'status', 'revenue']])

# Clean revenue: remove commas and convert to float
data['revenue_clean'] = data['revenue'].str.replace(',', '', regex=False).astype(float)

# Drop QA orders
data_clean = data[data['revenue_clean'] != 999999.99]

# Drop refunded orders (status == 'refunded')
data_clean = data_clean[data_clean['status'] == 'completed']

# Replace -1 in customer_age with NaN
data_clean['customer_age'] = data_clean['customer_age'].replace(-1, pd.NA)

# Final data shape
print(f"\nFinal data shape after cleaning: {data_clean.shape}")

# Summary of key metrics
print("\nConversion rate by channel:")
print(data_clean.groupby('channel')['converted'].mean())

print("\nAverage revenue by channel:")
print(data_clean.groupby('channel')['revenue_clean'].mean())

print("\nCustomer segment distribution:")
print(data_clean['customer_segment'].value_counts())"}
